articles.title: Adidas faces boycott calls over campaign featuring former Israeli soldier
articles.summary: Activists slam campaign showing soldier while over 5,000 Palestinians faced amputations due to Israeli attacks in Gaza.
articles.body:
Sportswear giant Adidas has faced criticism and calls for a boycott for featuring a former Israeli army soldier in an advertising campaign for the company’s single-shoe service for amputees.

The Adidas advertisement promoting its in-store service, which shows former Israeli soldier Shalev Biton trying on a shoe at a store in Israel and then wearing it while running outdoors, was termed “an affront to Palestinians” by a boycott campaigns coordinator on Sunday.

Biton lost his leg after being wounded during the 2021 Israel-Gaza conflict, during which the Israeli army attacked the besieged enclave repeatedly in an 11-day assault.

Human rights campaigners and pro-Palestine activists say the immediate outrage and online boycott campaign targeted at Adidas should not come as a surprise to the German athletic apparel and footwear company.

“This isn’t Adidas being tone-deaf or insensitive; it is an absolute affront to the Palestinians who have lost their loved ones, killed by Israel, and who have lost their limbs [to Israeli attacks],” Stephanie Westbrook, a sports boycott campaigns coordinator for the Palestinian Campaign for the Academic and Cultural Boycott of Israel (PACBI) – a founding member of the Boycott, Divestment, and Sanctions (BDS) movement – told Al Jazeera.

Westbrook underlined the danger of such campaigns, which she believes would “normalise Israel’s crimes against Palestinians and allow it to continue to commit them with impunity”.

“Here we have an Adidas campaign featuring an Israeli soldier, whose whole identity is centred around his being a soldier, who lost his leg while participating in one of the repeated Israeli assaults on Gaza, serving in an army of a state that is currently committing genocide, has carried out an illegal military occupation of the Palestinian territory, and that has been imposing a decades-long apartheid rule over Palestinians,” she said.

The World Health Organization estimates that between 5,000 and 6,000 people in Gaza have undergone amputations as of early October 2025, when Israel and Hamas signed a “ceasefire” agreement. They are among the 42,000 Palestinians in Gaza who have sustained life-changing injuries during the two-year conflict.

Nearly a year since the ceasefire, conditions remain dire due to Israel’s blockage of humanitarian aid from entering the enclave.

While the advertisement shows the soldier returning to the streets to exercise and run, more than one thousand Palestinian athletes have been killed during Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza.

Hundreds of aspiring footballers have lost their limbs and have formed amputee football teams, finding some respite in sport despite their pain.

These players hold on to football as a means of survival and are trying to reclaim fragments of their former lives despite months of loss, injuries, and widespread destruction.

Spanish actor Javier Bardem was among those calling for a boycott of the sportswear brand. Bardem, who is a vocal pro-Palestine activist, shared several images and videos highlighting the boycott campaign on his social media accounts.

US-Palestinian author Susan Abulhawa, Pakistani author Fatima Bhutto, and Palestinians on social media called for a boycott of Adidas products.

Rights campaigner Westbrook highlighted Israel’s blockade on Gaza, which prevents medicines and prosthetics from entering the Gaza Strip following Israeli destruction of the territory’s medical facilities.

Children account for a quarter of all amputations in Gaza over the past two years, making it the place in the world with the highest number of child amputees per capita, according to the International Rescue Committee.

Westbrook said Israel had “decimated the health sector”, causing a severe lack of care and rehabilitation services.

“Its medieval siege is preventing prosthetics from even entering Gaza, creating this man-made shortage,” she added.

Since the Israeli war on Gaza began in October 2023, reports the United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF), 42,000 Palestinians have suffered life-altering injuries, of which 11,000 are children.

articles.title: Wrestling Legend Bill Dundee Dies at 82, Memphis Wrestling Superstar Competed in AWA, WCW, More
articles.summary: Pro wrestling legend "Superstar" Bill Dundee died Sunday at the age of 82, WWE announced.
articles.body:
Pro wrestling legend "Superstar" Bill Dundee died Sunday at the age of 82, WWE announced.

Per TMZ , Dundee's son, former wrestler Jamie Dundee, aka J.C. Ice, announced on Facebook that his father died at approximately 3:30 a.m. on Sunday. A cause of death has not been publicly disclosed.

TMZ noted that Dunee "had also dealt with serious health issues in recent years," and "his son previously revealed that the wrestling legend had been diagnosed with dementia."

Born as William Cruickshanks in Scotland and raised in Australia, Dundee started wrestling in his home country in the 1960s before traveling to the United States years later. He became a key figure in the wrestling scene in Memphis for his work alongside Jerry "The King" Lawler, who was his biggest rival as well as his former tag team partner, winning the AWA World Tag Team Championship twice.

In addition to his work inside the ring, Dundee worked as a booker in several wrestling territories for decades. He had a brief run in the NWA's Jim Crockett Promotions as well as a stint in WCW in 1993-94.

Dundee was inducted into the Memphis Wrestling Hall of Fame in 2017, and he wrestled his final match two years later.

Just one day before his passing, Dundee was honored during Saturday's episode of Memphis Wrestling, with members of the roster greeting him and paying tribute to him throughout the show.

articles.title: China GT crash: Driver Ollie Millropy says Loek Hartog saved his life in car fire
articles.summary: British racing driver Ollie Millroy says he is only alive thanks to a rival who pulled him from the burning wreckage of his car following a crash at the China GT.
articles.body:
A British racing driver says he is only alive thanks to a rival who pulled him from the burning wreckage of a car.

Dutchman Loek Hartog abandoned his own vehicle during the China GT Championship race in Shanghai and doused the flames of Ollie Millroy's Ferrari with a fire extinguisher before dragging him from the vehicle.

"I am still alive tonight, entirely thanks to one man," Millroy said in a post on Instagram.

"Loek Hartog stopped instantly with no flag marshals or fire crews in sight, and risked his own life to get me out of the car."

Organisers said in statement they "will further review and investigate the accident and formulate more comprehensive plans to address shortcomings in competition organisation, support, emergency response, rescue and medical services".

Millroy's team, AAI Motorsport, said it "will no longer participate in any races organised by China GT" in a statement that was hugely critical of safety standards at Saturday's race and accused the organisers of negligence.

"I don't remember anything between 30 seconds before the crash and one hour after it, but I will remember his incredible act of bravery for the rest of my life," Millroy said.

"One day I will tell our three kids this story and Loek will be the biggest superhero in history in their eyes too."

Millroy said he suffered five broken ribs, a broken collar bone, broken hand, broken finger and bruised lung in the crash, adding: "It could have been much worse."

"Thank you Loek. I owe you my life for your selfless act."

Replying to the post, Hartog said: "I am so thankful to have been right at the place I needed to be in space and time."

He later wrote in his own post on Instagram: "When I saw a car turning into a huge fireball far ahead, there wasn't really a decision to make.

"From what I had seen, I genuinely believed the driver might not be able to get out by himself. I stopped, got out and went towards the car. There was never a moment of doubt.

"It was scary. There were moments where I didn't know I would actually be able to get Ollie out.

"But this isn't about what I did, and I'm sure many people in the same position would have reacted exactly the same way."

AAI Motorsport said Millroy's car "continued to burn for more than a minute" after the accident and that "no timely and effective firefighting and rescue operations were seen".

It said: "What might have happened if that driver hadn't stepped up today?

"We accept the inherent dangers of motorsports, but we absolutely cannot accept a driver being exposed to avoidable death."

articles.title: Galán y Chingotto siguen soñando con el número 1 tras coronarse en Madrid en una final épica
articles.standfirst: Séptimo título para los chicos de Jorge Martínez, que derrotaron a Coki Nieto y Mike Yanguas en el Movistar Arena
articles.summary: Séptimo título para los chicos de Jorge Martínez, que derrotaron a Coki Nieto y Mike Yanguas en una final brutal en el Movistar Arena
articles.body: Ale Galán y Federico Chingotto se proclamaron campeones del Comunidad de Madrid P1 de Premier Padel 2026 tras tumbar en la final a Mike Yanguas y Coki Nieto con el resultado de 6-4, 5-7 y 6-4 que se traduce en su séptimo título de la temporada 2026. La dupla española, que vivía su primera final como pareja y que venían de cargarse el viernes a los favoritos Coello y Tapia, dio la cara hasta el final pero acabó sucumbiendo ante dos jugadores que ansían el número 1… y que no han desaprovechado la oportunidad presentada para recortar puntos y acercarse un poco más en el ránking. Coki y Mike salieron fuertes desde el inicio, sin complejos y mirando de tú a tú a la cara a los aspirantes a reyes del pádel. Sin embargo, en el ecuador de la primera manga, que acabó 6-4, Chingotto y Galán asestaron el primer golpe en la que sería la única rotura. Era 3-3, y un star point puso por delante a los de Jorge Martínez, que no fallaron en su servicio y se metieron en el bolsillo el primer round. En el segundo, ‘Chingalán’ estuvo a punto de seguir con la inercia del primero, pero Mike y Coki no se dejaron ir y salvaron hasta cuatro bolas de rotura. Y por ahí caminó el resto del set, con las dos parejas defendiendo su saque hasta que en el noveno juego, con 4-4, la historia se repitió. Nuevo break cuando tocaba, 5-4 con saque a favor… pero Yanguas y Nieto no se dieron por vencidos. Cuando todo parecía abocado al final, consiguieron su primer break del partido, igualaron de nuevo el set… y volvieron a romper para mandar la batalla al tercer set. 5-7… y partido nuevo. El tercero siguió ajustado a más no poder. Con Coki y Yanguas salvando multitud de bolas de break, manteniendo el barco a flote… hasta el noveno juego, cuando ‘Chingalán’ asestó el golpe definitivo. La primera rotura del tercer set llegó cuando más lo necesitaban, y ya con su servicio pusieron el lazo a un partido antológico que hizo vibrar como nunca a la capital de España. 6-4 y campeonato tras más de dos horas y media de batalla. Con este resultado, Ale y Fede se quedan a 470 puntos en la Race 2026 de Coello y Tapia e incluso ganando el Major de París de la próxima semana en Roland Garros podrían superarles. Suceda lo que suceda, lo que está claro es que los de Jorge Martínez no se van a rendir y que la pelea está más que abierta. Queda mucho.

articles.title: Super League: Wigan captain Liam Farrell announces plan to retire at end of 2026 season
articles.summary: 'It's been a whirlwind of a career, more than I could ever have dreamed of doing,' says one-club man who is set to retire after 428 appearances for Wigan; skipper will hope to add a seventh Super League title next month
articles.body:
The 36-year-old, who has only ever played for the Warriors, will call time on a career which has spanned 17 professional seasons. Farrell has captained Wigan since 2023 and been capped 12 times by England.

He has totalled 428 appearances for Wigan and scored 151 tries, winning six Super League titles, five Challenge Cups and two World Club Challenge successes during his illustrious career.

Wigan will play their final league game of the season against Catalans on Friday before beginning their play-off campaign, live on Sky Sports.

In an emotional video posted on social media, Farrell shared images from his time at Wigan and thanked team-mates and supporters.

Farrell said: "It's been a whirlwind of a career, more than I could ever have dreamed of doing.

"Although I'll be sad not to be playing anymore, I'm also very grateful for the career that I have had and I can now look forward to the next part of my life."

He added: "You have to make the right call at the right time, and I think I have done that. Speaking to people close to me, professionals and the advice I have been given, it's the right time.

"Playing one game for Wigan was always the goal for me. If I had have done that and never played again I'd have been immensely proud, my family would have been proud and we'd have gone back to being Wigan fans.

"So to have been able to play over 400 games in this jersey has been nothing short of incredible."

Wigan's chief executive Kris Radlinski confirmed Farrell will remain in a role with the club, saying: "Liam will go down as one of Wigan's greatest players. Sustaining excellence for so many years requires extraordinary commitment, resilience and mental strength.

"He has always put the team first, carried himself with quiet humility, and earned the respect of everyone connected with the club. His legacy is secure and he deserves to be celebrated.

"Liam will remain at the club in an S&C capacity after gaining his qualifications alongside his playing career. Alongside this role, his knowledge and experience will help develop the next generation of Warriors leaders."

Wigan boss Matt Peet added: "Anyone who's watched Wigan over the last 17 years will know what Liam Farrell means to the Club.

"The way he's played, the trophies he's lifted, moments in big games, times he's played injured or out of position, and always carried himself impeccably.

articles.title: Burghley Horse Trials: Gemma Stevens claims biggest win of 25-year career
articles.summary: Britain's Gemma Stevens claims the biggest win of her 25-year career with victory at Burghley Horse Trials.
articles.body:
Britain's Gemma Stevens won the Burghley Horse Trials for the first time on Sunday, the biggest victory of her career on her 31st attempt at five-star level.

The 41-year-old Olympian, riding Chilli Knight, cemented victory in executing a faultless showjumping round to finish on her dressage score of 29.6 - the only rider in the field to do so.

Compatriot Katie Magee finished second on Treworra, with USA's Caroline Pamukcu and HSH Blake in third.

"It's only taken me 25 years and finally I've managed to win a big B [Burghley or Badminton]. I couldn't be more proud," Stevens said.

Stevens, who first competed at the level in 2007, previously rode Chilli Knight's mother, King's Gem.

"It's unbelievable, I've known him [Chilli Knight] since the day he was born and this honestly means the absolute world," she said.

The win is redemption for Stevens after a disappointing World Championships in Aachen, Germany last month, when she failed to complete the cross-county event for the British team.

"Aachen was really tough, but that's sport. You've got to just bounce back and get on with it," she added.

Stevens and Chilli Knight previously won the replacement five-star event at Bicton in 2021, after Covid cancelled Burghley.

articles.summary: Substitute Federico Gatti scores a stoppage-time goal to earn Juventus a draw against AC Milan and extend their unbeaten start to the Serie A season.
articles.body:
Substitute Federico Gatti scored a stoppage-time goal to earn Juventus a draw against AC Milan and extend their unbeaten start to the Serie A season.

Juve dominated the first half at Allianz Stadium and were denied by three fine saves from Milan goalkeeper Mike Maignan.

The visitors took a surprise lead when Alphadjo Cisse became the first player to score against Juventus this season.

However, defender Gatti connected with Teun Koopmeiners' cross to emphatically head home and prevent former Manchester United boss Ruben Amorim from becoming Milan's first manager since 1958 to win his opening three league games.

Juventus, for whom new loan signing Omari Hutchinson was an unused substitute, are fifth in the table and Milan fourth.

articles.title: Gatti salvages Juve draw with AC Milan in Serie A
articles.summary: Federico Gatti came off the bench and scored an injury-time equaliser as Juventus snatched a 1-1 draw with AC Milan in Serie A on Sunday.Parma and Monza got...
articles.body:
Federico Gatti came off the bench and scored an injury-time equaliser as Juventus snatched a 1-1 draw with AC Milan in Serie A on Sunday.

Both teams arrived at the Allianz Stadium after starting the season with back-to-back wins and remained unbeaten after a hard-fought affair.

The result leaves Roma and Inter Milan as the two teams with 100 percent records after three games, with Lazio attempting to join them when they face Udinese on Monday.

"We didn't deserve to win, and Juve didn't deserve to lose," Milan coach Ruben Amorim told DAZN.

"We lost possession too often and didn't play well, but we've only been working together for two months."

Juve coach Luciano Spalletti was critical of Randal Kolo Muani after he missed several chances in their first match of the season against Frosinone.

But he insisted he still has faith in the France striker, despite his wait to get off the mark in his second spell at the club.

"I chose him to lead our attack and I am sticking with that choice," said Spalletti.

"I will stick with it until the end of the season, and we'll see then just how far he has taken us."

Juventus had the better of the first half but visiting goalkeeper Mike Maignan made an excellent save to keep out Francisco Conceicao's shot from their clearest chance.

The Portugal winger went even closer 10 minutes into the second period, but fired his effort off the base of the post after being found by Manuel Locatelli.

Milan grabbed the lead in the 68th minute with their first shot on target of the match.

After Juve striker Randal Kolo Muani was left on the ground appealing for a free-kick, the away side broke.

Samuel Chukwueze fed 19-year-old substitute Alphadjo Cisse, who cut inside and swept a low finish past Juve goalkeeper Guglielmo Vicario and into the bottom corner.

Juve brought on Nick Woltemade with 15 minutes left for his debut after joining on loan from Newcastle on deadline day.

But it was another substitute who rescued the hosts a point, as centre-back Gatti powered a header in off the bar from Teun Koopmeiners's free-kick.

Frosinone made it consecutive victories as Georgia international Giorgi Kvernadze's late goal grabbed them a dramatic 3-2 win over fellow promoted side Venezia.

Parma and Monza got their first points of the season in a 1-1 draw, while Artem Dovbyk's injury-time strike also got Bologna on the board for the campaign with a 2-2 draw against Sassuolo.

articles.title: Alcaraz breezes into last eight at US Open
articles.summary: Carlos Alcaraz beats American Tommy Paul in straight sets to reach US Open quarterfinals.
articles.body:
Carlos Alcaraz beat American 20th seed Tommy Paul 6-4, 6-3, 6-4 in a high-voltage tennis hit-fest on Sunday to reach the US Open quarterfinals and remain firmly on track for back-to-back titles at Flushing Meadows.

The seven-time Grand Slam champion hit top form in New York after nearly five months out with a right wrist injury, and extended his major match-winning streak to 18 with a stunning display of shotmaking against a fellow big-hitter.

“I think I just played my game,” Alcaraz said. “I tried to play to my style. Tommy’s such a talented player, and his shots are pretty dangerous, and it’s difficult to control the ball when it comes to you. I was ready for a battle.

“I was trying to be aggressive all the time … I did well to put pressure on his return, which helped me stay calm and to think clearly. I was really happy with the performance.”

Alcaraz’s serve came under pressure in the third game when Paul fired an exquisite 161km/hour (100 mph) forehand winner around the net that brought Arthur Ashe Stadium to its feet. Still, the Spaniard stood firm before striking late to snatch the opening set.

The 23-year-old left a vapour trail with a crosscourt winner to carve out an early opening in the second set and swiftly took a 2-0 lead, before trading breaks with Paul and breezing through the remaining games for a commanding lead.

Even with much of the show-court crowd yearning for a home winner, second seed Alcaraz continued to steal the show with his audacious play, moving to the brink of improving his win-loss record against American players at the Grand Slams to 13-0.

After shifting down to cruise mode, Alcaraz briefly flinched at the finish line, but he regrouped to deliver the knockout blow and set up a meeting with American Ben Shelton or Greek Stefanos Tsitsipas in the next round.

Alcaraz hit a rocket of a forehand to bring up match point, another sign that he was reaching the peak of his powers at a venue where he has thrived ever since his maiden Grand Slam triumph four years ago.

“I think so,” Alcaraz said when asked about being back to his best in New York, where he has reached the quarterfinals in five of his six appearances now.

“It shows how special this place is to me; I’m just enjoying myself on court here. It doesn’t matter that I was out for over four months. Every time I come here, I play well.”

articles.title: New York Giants 2026 NFL Season Preview: The Top 5 Burning Questions
articles.summary: We’re just days away from the New York Giants‘ 2026 season opener against the Dallas Cowboys at MetLife Stadium. This […]
articles.body:
We're just days away from the New York Giants ' 2026 season opener against the Dallas Cowboys at MetLife Stadium.

This is a pivotal year in the history of the Giants franchise as they feel they have finally found the right guy to lead the organization in head coach John Harbaugh . New York has made upgrades this offseason in all three phases of the game and to the coaching staff.

But you never know how the additions are going to work until the team takes the field. Here are the top five burning questions for Big Blue heading into the season.

The biggest question surrounding the Giants heading into the season is when Malik Nabers will see his first action since tearing his ACL in October. Ever since it was revealed that he had a second surgery on his knee, there have been concerns about whether he'll be ready for the start of the season.

Although he's participated throughout training camp, as of right now it's not a lock that he'll be on the field for Week 1. He will eventually make his 2026 debut in the early part of the season. But then the question becomes: what will he look like when he's back on the field?

If he's playing like one of the best wideouts in the league he was prior to his injury, the Giants will have one of the best offenses in the NFC. If he's compromised by the injury, the Giants won't have a true number one wideout, and the offense will have a short ceiling.

How big of a leap can Jaxson Dart make in year two?

There's a ton of optimism surrounding Jaxson Dart as he enters his second season in the NFL. Most quarterbacks make their biggest leap from year one to year two, and considering Dart had 24 total touchdowns with five interceptions, some feel the sky is the limit.

However, he is learning a new system under new offensive coordinator Matt Nagy, where he'll be in the shotgun less frequently than he did in 2025. Early on in training camp, he and the offense struggled, but gradually got better as the summer progressed.

If Dart has a firm grasp of the offense, New York can be a playoff team in 2026 if he can stay healthy.

Will the run defense be better under Dennard Wilson?

The run defense was the weakest part of the team last season. The Giants allowed 145.3 yards per game, which was 31 st in the league.

The team traded Dexter Lawrence to the Cincinnati Bengals and replaced him by signing DJ Reader, and also added Shelby Harris to beef up the defensive line. But the biggest addition to the defense might be defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson, who has emphasized the importance of stopping the run from day one. In his final year with the Tennessee Titans in 2025, the Titans had the 15th-ranked run defense.

If the run defense can be middle of the pack, it will bode well for the team's chances this season. If they're still unable to stop the run, it will be another long season for Big Blue.

Will the corners be able to handle elite wideouts?

Throughout the summer, Greg Newsome, Paulson Adebo, Deonte Banks and rookie Colton Hood have all played with the first-team defense during training camp. Right now, we don't know for certain who will be the two starting outside corners, but whoever the duo is, they'll be challenged early.

In the season opener, they'll face the Cowboys, who had the second-ranked passing offense in 2025. Dallas has arguably the best wide receiver tandem in CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens . Last year, the duo combined for 168 receptions, for 2,506 yards with 12 touchdowns.

Things don't get any easier for New York in Week 2 when they travel to Los Angeles to take on the Rams . The Rams had the number one passing attack in 2025, led by reigning league MVP Matthew Stafford . Stafford's top two targets, Puka Nacua and Davante Adams , combined for 189 receptions, 2,504 yards, and 24 touchdowns.

In addition to the first two games of the year, the Giants will face elite receivers throughout the season. The corners must show that they can hold their own in order for the team to have a winning season.

Will the new additions live up to the hype?

Big Blue has received high praise for the additions they made to the team this offseason in free agency and the 2026 NFL Draft. In the draft, they took Arvell Reese , who they felt was the best defensive player in the class, and then selected Francis Mauigoa with the 10 th pick to play right guard to solidify the offensive line.

The biggest acquisitions the team made in free agency were Isaiah Likely, Darnell Mooney, Tremaine Edmunds, and Jordan Stout. Then in June, the team brought back Odell Beckham Jr . At first, people outside the organization may have thought OBJ was washed, but he showed throughout training camp and the preseason that he can still create separation and get open.

Due to these additions, and being led by a Super Bowl-winning head coach, there's optimism that the franchise is headed in the right direction. If they can live up to the hype surrounding their signing, New York will have its first winning season since 2022.

articles.body:

articles.title: Game Thread: Twins (68-74) at White Sox (74-68)
articles.summary: South Siders line up for another Sunday rubber match against division rivals
articles.body:
The White Sox are set to conclude their season series against the Minnesota Twins under the bright lights of Sunday Night Baseball. Bryan Hudson will be the opener for the Sox, his eighth time appearing in the role this year. He's been largely effective to this point, allowing three earned runs over eight innings leading off a game, with five of those seven stints being scoreless.

It's a selection of opener that would seem to indicate a confidence in him beyond the simple platoon advantage, as the Twins 2-3-4 hitters will all be facing Hudson from the right side. Manager Derek Shelton is alternating his lefties and righties at the bottom of the lineup, so given that José Urquidy lines up as today's logical bulk man despite being on somewhat short rest, it might not be surprising to see Will Venable try to stretch Hudson for two innings to start things out against this lineup:

Venable counters with the team's A-lineup, so to speak, against soft-tossing righthander Bailey Ober. He's found a solid level of success against the Sox in the past, holding them to two runs (one earned) over five innings just last week, and running an overall 3.56 ERA in 16 starts countering the Pale Hose, the most he's ever seen of one team. Chase Meidroth and Colson Montgomery have both notched homers against him, so having already connected on homers in consecutive games, a hope for what has already seemingly become a patented homer binge from Montgomery may be alive and well.

This is a Sox lineup that has zero postseason experience beyond platooner Andrew Benintendi and, if you want to count it, Munetaka Murakami in his native Japan. Playing in prime time on national TV doesn't exactly have the same caché in baseball as the prestige of being featured on Sunday or Monday Night Football, but NBC's decision to flex the Sox to this game should be taken with some pride. Does anyone care to guess the date of the last time the South Siders played a) on Sunday night b) at home c) while in first place?

At least we'll have a friendly face in the booth. While I certainly wouldn't want Jason Benetti to push the boundaries of his professionalism, there is a real part of me that wants to judge, by his approach to tonight's game, whether we have any long-term hope of what would probably be the most joyous Chicago sports reunion since the words "I'm back" hit the newswires.

First pitch will be broadcast on NBC and Peacock at 5:20 p.m. CT. though Len Kasper and Darrin Jackson will be there with their usual radio broadcast on WMVP AM 1000. See you in the comments!

articles.title: Will Puka Nacua play in Week 1? Rams insider delivers crucial update on star receiver
articles.summary: Puka Nacua is expected to play in the Rams’ season opener. The star receiver has been dealing with a psoas injury, but the signs out of Los Angeles are posit...
articles.body:
Puka Nacua is expected to play in the Rams' season opener. The star receiver has been dealing with a psoas injury, but the signs out of Los Angeles are positive.

The Rams meet the 49ers in Australia in Week 1, a game played on the other side of the world. Nacua has spent weeks managing the injury, but he is back in stride.

ESPN's Jeremy Fowler delivered the update on SportsCenter.

Fowler: Rams expect Nacua to play in the opener

"They're banged up, they're bringing everybody to Australia. They're hoping that everybody can play," Fowler said.

"Puka Nacua has a psoas injury. You don't hear that very often. They held him out for a few weeks, taken it easy with him. He's been back in stride this week. No setbacks."

"I'm hearing that the Rams expect him to play. So, you should have Matthew Stafford, Puka, Davante Adams in that vaunted passing game now."

It is exactly the news Rams fans wanted. The extra time at home during their travel preparation has given Nacua a chance to heal.

Head coach Sean McVay is optimistic too.

"Been hitting some high speed yards at a really good clip with Reggie [Scott] and his group," McVay said. "And when we get back out there, it'll be fun to have him."

There is also no suspension incoming for the receiver, despite his off-field issues this summer, leaving him available for the curtain raiser.

The timing matters beyond Week 1. Nacua is entering a contract season on his four-year, $4.1 million rookie-scale deal.

He led the NFL in receptions and yards per catch in 2025 and narrowly missed Offensive Player of the Year to Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who has since reset the market with a $120 million deal in Seattle.

Nacua, a two-time Pro Bowler and First Team All-Pro, has more than outplayed his draft slot. A big season, healthy and available, sets him up for a market-resetting extension.

First things first. The game in Australia kicks off on Netflix, and the Rams' most important receiver is expected to be in the line-up.

articles.title: Giants, Jon Runyan reach agreement on two-year, $22 million contract extension
articles.summary: The Giants agreed to a two-year, $22 million contract extension with guard Jon Runyan on Sunday, reports ESPN's Adam Schefter.
articles.body:
The Giants agreed to a two-year, $22 million contract extension with guard Jon Runyan on Sunday, reports ESPN's Adam Schefter.

The deal, which includes $21.5 million guaranteed, will take the 29-year-old, who has spent the last two seasons in New York, through the 2028 season.

After beginning his career with the Green Bay Packers where he played for four seasons, Runyan became a free agent in 2024 and signed a three-year, $30 million contract to join Big Blue.

With the Giants, Runyan played in 16 games (all starts) in 2025 after playing 13 games (all starts) the year before and has been a steady presence in a somewhat shaky offensive line.

The 6-foot-4, 307-pounder will look to better protect quarterback Jaxson Dart this season after Dart was sacked 35 times in 14 games during his rookie campaign.

articles.title: Early kickoff return TD sets tone as Prairie View A&M routs rival Texas Southern
articles.summary: Unlike last year's thrilled decided on a walk-off, Prairie View A&M rolled past Texas Southern with a big third quarter.
articles.body:
PRAIRIE VIEW - Last year's Labor Day Classic was not decided until the final play. On Sunday at Panther Stadium, Prairie View's Jahbari Kuykendall returned the opening kickoff 90 yards for a touchdown, setting off a range of emotions from both teams and their fan bases.

That is the Texas Southern-Prairie View A&M rivalry in a nutshell. Exciting games are the norm. From start to finish.

Prairie View won last year's matchup on a walk-off touchdown. Sunday's game was not as close. And again, the outcome favored the Panthers.

The Panthers came out firing and did not let up in routing TSU 52-14 in a game that was nationally televised on ESPN2.

After leading 17-7 at halftime, Prairie View (1-1) outscored TSU 28-0 in the third quarter.

Quarterback Tevin Carter passed for four scores - two to Travon Jones - and ran for another in directing the Panthers' offense under second-year coach Tremaine Jackson.

An hour after kickoff, the game was stopped at noon due to lightning in the area. After a 57-minute delay, the game resumed with the Panthers holding a 17-0 advantage with 12:35 left before the half.

A junior from Westside, Kuykendall got the SWAC game off to an electric beginning. Kuykendall caught the ball in the middle of the field at his 10-yard line. He immediately veered to his left and followed a wall of blockers into the end zone.

On PV's first offensive possession, Carter connected with Damien McDaniel on a 24-yard scoring pass. Less than five minutes in, the Panthers were ahead 14-0.

Ethan Eddings' 37-yard field goal with eight seconds remaining in the opening quarter pushed the Panthers' lead to 17-0.

In the third quarter, the Panthers blew the game open. Carter threw scoring strikes of 54 yards to Chase Bingmon coming out of the backfield, and 39 yards to a wide-open Jones, putting PV up 38-7.

Linebacker Tyler Morehead came up with a big fumble recovery deep in PV territory late in the first half for the Panthers, who were clinging to a 10-point advantage.

Defensive end Dorian Gates also recovered a fumble for the Panthers, who opened their season last week in a tough 49-30 loss at Tarleton State .

Special teams provided another bright spot for the Panthers. Corey Thompson Jr. and Rondell Carter were outstanding on kickoff return coverage.

Quarterback Cam'Ron McCoy scored on a 17-yard run for TSU (1-1), which got 85 rushing yards from Athean Renfro Jr.

McCoy, who did not complete his first pass until midway of the second quarter, displayed his running ability with a long run of 35 yards.

Texas Southern holds a 45-36-1 advantage in the series, but Prairie View has won 19 of the past 23 matchups.

The Panthers won last year's meeting 22-21 , scoring on a 17-yard pass as time expired from Cameron Peters to Rodny Ojo in Jackson's first game as Panthers coach.

Both teams go on the road against FBS opponents this Saturday. Texas Southern visits UTEP while Prairie View takes on Baylor.

articles.title: How Charlie Woods fared in final round of Junior Players Championship
articles.summary: Charlie Woods tied for eighth at the Junior Players Championship, marking his best national finish since 2025.
articles.body:
Charlie Woods enjoyed his best finish of the 2026 season this weekend at the Junior Players Championship.

Woods, a senior at the Benjamin School and son of legendary golfer Tiger Woods , shot 71 (1-under) in the final round on Sunday, Sept. 6 at TPC Sawgrass in Ponte Vedra Beach, Florida.

He finished at 1-under overall and tied for eighth across the three-round event. JP Lynch of Austin, Texas won the event at 8-under.

Woods finished his tournament with the type of round that has been characteristic of his tournament appearance, offsetting five birdies with four bogeys. Overall, he carded 14 birdies and 13 bogeys in the event.

Here are some highlights from his final round:

On No. 10, Woods nearly holed out his approach shot for an eagle and carded birdie.

On No. 11, he sunk a 15-foot birdie putt to pull into the tournament top 10.

After a par on No. 12, he ran into tough luck, lipping out on birdie putts at No. 13, 14 and 15.

On No. 16, he hooked his tee shot deep into the trees and punched out to later save par.

On the famous "Island Green," Woods played long and left, two-putting from 25 feet.

The Junior Players Championship will go down as undeniable success for Woods. It's his best finish in a junior golf tournament with a national field since he won the 2025 Team TaylorMade Invitational at Streamsong Resort (Black) in Bowling Green, Florida.

Woods also made news on Friday by signing with one of the world's biggest golf brands. He formally announced an NIL contract with TaylorMade via social media with multiple promotional videos.

Final: Out 37, In 34, Total 71 (1-under)

Eric J. Wallace is deputy sports editor for The Palm Beach Post. He can be reached at ejwallace@usatodayco.com.

Florida Times Union reporter Garry Smits contributed to this report.

articles.title: Despite star power, can Cowboys defense outperform Rams in long run?
articles.summary: The Cowboys have done a lot to revamp their defense, not with big names but quality players and depth.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys and Los Angeles Rams have two of the more dangerous offenses in the entire NFL, but they both had significant defensive issues to address this offseason. The two clubs went going about making their fixes in different ways. While the Rams made big moves, the Cowboys took a more subtle approach. Was it ultimately the more logical and better one?

Here's why the Cowboys' approach might just put them in a better position than the Rams in 2026.

Despite all the defensive hype Dallas has built throughout the offseason, it has been overshadowed by the Rams' manuevers. The additions of Myles Garrett, Trent McDuffie, and recently un-retired Aaron Donald make the Rams a formidable defense on paper, but the Cowboys have made significant changes of their own. After hiring Christian Parker as defensive coordinator, Dallas replaced 17 of its 26 defensive players from last season, a 70% roster turnover.

While the Rams' wide-sweeping changes caught everyone off guard, the Cowboys' defensive overhaul was expected after finishing the 2025 season dead last in both pass defense and scoring defense.

Parker's roster building approach was two-pronged: rather than targeting the biggest names in free agency or on the trade market, he focused on adding quality starters who fit specific roles within his defensive scheme. More importantly, Parker prioritized rebuilding their depth at all three levels. Their emphasis on depth could help Dallas withstand the inevitable injuries that face teams, perhaps better than the Rams, who are currently viewed as favorites to represent the NFC in the Super Bowl.

Los Angeles lost several depth players at every level of the defense and is counting on its star additions to offset those departures. But those expectations could quickly change if one of those stars goes down. Garrett is already reportedly dealing with knee swelling and lower-body soreness and has not practiced for several weeks. Losing Garrett at any point during the season could significantly impact the Rams' defense.

The same can't be said about the Cowboys.

Dallas' depth is what gives the defense its best chance to surprise the rest of the NFL. Parker built a versatile secondary loaded with young talent , including Caleb Downs, Shavon Revel Jr., Ameer Speed, and Alijah Clark, while adding proven veterans such as Jalen Thompson and Cobie Durant to play with DaRon Bland and Malik Hooker, stabilizing the group. On the defensive line, the Cowboys now have an improved rotation with Rashan Gary, Donovan Ezeiruaku, Von Miller, James Houston, Kenny Clark, Quinnen Williams, Jonathan Bullard, and Osa Odighizuwa, without a significant drop-off in production.

The Rams may have more star power at the top of the roster, but Dallas has assembled a deeper and more balanced defensive unit. The Cowboys' depth could prove more valuable than any one superstar and ultimately be the difference between simply having a talented defense and fielding one capable of making a championship run.

articles.title: Czech Darts Open: Luke Littler topples Luke Humphries 8-6 in final on return to European Tour in Prague
articles.summary: Littler beats Humphries 8-6 in final after beating Michael van Gerwen, Danny Noppert and Krzysztof Ratajski earlier on Sunday; Sky Sports remains the home of darts with the World Grand Prix coming up from September 28-October 4
articles.body:
Littler had not played in a European Tour event since March, but roared to glory with an 8-6 victory in Sunday night's final to end his opponent's hopes of winning this title for a third straight year.

Littler hit five 180s and averaged just over 95 as both players struggled in the heat at the PVA EXPO after a long day which had already seen The Nuke overcome Michael van Gerwen in the semi-finals, Danny Noppert in the quarter-finals and Krzysztof Ratajski in the last 16.

"It's good to be back and I'm back with a bang," said Littler after his victory.

World No 1 Littler won the first two legs against world No 2 Humphries in Sunday's final, only to see his rival, who has reached four of the last five finals in this tournament, reel off three straight legs to take the lead.

Littler fought back to move ahead with a 130 checkout in the ninth leg - the biggest finish of the game - and then won the next two legs to move 7-4 ahead in a race to eight.

Humphries rallied to win the next two legs and was millimetres away from sending the game to a decider, as he wired two darts at D16.

Littler recovered to pin D10 to win this tournament for the first time, taking home the £35,000 first prize and guaranteeing his place at the European Championship in Dortmund in October.

That's one of the titles that Littler wants to win as he eyes a clean sweep of major trophies in 2026 - and it means he's unlikely to play in any other regular European Tour events this season.

"I'm not sure now I've won this one," he explained. "I think I've secured my place in Dortmund. That's obviously the one I'm chasing.

"In two weeks time it's the World Series in Amsterdam. We'll have to see what happens, what the plan is and how busy I am."

Humphries had overcome Gerwyn Price, William O'Connor and Andrew Gilding earlier on Sunday to reach the final for the third year in a row, but he was not upset at missing out on a 'three-peat'.

"I can't be upset," he said. "The two darts I threw at D16 were right on the wire and if that goes in, it could have been a different game.

"That's just the way it goes. He's a fantastic player. I've been playing here and there, not so great. Maybe good sometimes. I've got to dedicate my life a bit more to get better and keep pushing him.

"I keep saying I'm not beating him in finals so I've got to change things to keep matching him.

"I think he enjoys the challenge and I love it as well. Hopefully over the next four months, I push him and if he does the clean sweep [of major titles] he has to do it the hard way."
